question: What are the objectives of vertical-shaft alignment?
answer:
The objectives of vertical-shaft alignment are:

• The shaft would be straight,  
• The thrust runner would be perpendicular to the shaft,  
• The generator rotor and turbine would be round and concentric with the shaft,  
• The thrust bearing shoes would be level and equally loaded,  
• The stator, turbine seal rings, and guide bearings would be round, and  
• Their centerlines would be concentric and plumb.  

These objectives are outlined in FIST Volume 2-1 Alignment of Rotating Machinery, page 24 [1].

In this perfectly aligned unit, loading on the guide bearings would come primarily from any imbalance in the machine. Perfection is not possible. Because manufacturing, fabrication, and measurement all introduce inaccuracies, and precise adjustments are not always possible, there will be deviations from a perfect alignment. The farther the alignment deviates from perfection, the more stress is introduced to the unit. The following information uses terminology for the alignment of a motor to a pump because these components most often require alignment at Reclamation facilities. 5.1 Horizontal Shaft Alignment Horizontal pumps are typically coupled to the pump driver with a flexible coupling. The amount of misalignment a flexible coupling can tolerate depends on the design and characteristics, such as speed and torque, of the machines being coupled. The coupling’s manufacturer should provide installation instructions indicating the allowable tolerances for a particular design. A horizontal pump usually can be aligned acceptably by either the face and rim method or the reverse indicator method.
